title: New trial aims to advance research into Strep A vaccine development
content: An Australian human‑challenge trial is underway in Melbourne to accelerate research into a vaccine for group A streptococcal (Strep A) disease. The study, a partnership between Murdoch Children’s Research Institute (MCRI) and Doherty Clinical Trials Limited, will inoculate healthy adult volunteers with a defined strain of Strep A in a controlled setting. The trial builds on a previously validated human‑challenge model that MCRI reported as safe and suitable for vaccine testing. Strep A infections affect about 750 million people worldwide and cause more than 500 000 deaths each year, exceeding the mortality of influenza, typhoid and whooping cough. While most infections resolve, severe invasive disease such as toxic‑shock syndrome, necrotising fasciitis and post‑infectious conditions (acute rheumatic fever, rheumatic heart disease, kidney disease) can be fatal. MCRI’s Dr. Josh Osowicki said a vaccine would be a “global game‑changer” and added, 'A Strep A vaccine would not only prevent Strep A infections but also prevent invasive Strep A disease, which can be devastating for adults and children, like Asi who has been left with major communication and mobility issues,' he said. Doherty Clinical Trials CEO Dr. Andrew Brockway noted, 'Human challenge trials are an essential part of the global infectious‑disease toolkit, and the ability to conduct a study such as this positions Australia among a select group of countries capable of conducting these complex, high‑impact studies,' he said. Chief Medical Officer Professor James McCarthy added, 'Our facility was specifically designed so that we can safely conduct these important studies with a range of appropriate challenge models. Our staff are well trained to carefully expose participants to Strep A under close medical oversight. Doing these types of studies will accelerate the development of new vaccines and treatments that could save lives globally. We are proud to lead this pioneering initiative with the MCRI team, which will help fast‑track the development of Strep A therapeutics and vaccines both in Australia and overseas,' he said.

title: 肺鏈疫苗明年升級》有效應對血清型轉移 提升肺鏈施打率是關鍵 - 生活 - 自由時報電子報
content: The article discusses the upcoming upgrade of the pneumococcal vaccine in Taiwan, scheduled for 2026, to effectively address serotype replacement caused by widespread childhood vaccination. Since the introduction of the PCV13 vaccine for children ten years ago, there has been a significant reduction in severe pneumococcal infections, particularly among children, and a corresponding indirect protective effect observed in elderly populations. However, as seen in the U.S. experience, the widespread use of childhood vaccines has led to serotype replacement—where non-vaccine serotypes become more prevalent. To combat this, advanced countries such as the U.S., Canada, and EU nations have adopted PCV20 and PCV21 as priority vaccines for older adults and high-risk groups. In Taiwan, the Ministry of Health and Welfare’s Infectious Disease Prevention Advisory Committee, in a meeting held in September 2025, decided that individuals aged 19 to 64 with high-risk conditions who have completed a PCV13/15 and PPV23 series before age 65 may receive a booster dose of PCV20 or PCV21 within five years. The article emphasizes that increasing pneumococcal vaccination rates, especially among high-risk groups, is critical to maintaining public health protection.

title: 肺鏈疫苗明年升級》迎戰肺鏈新興血清型 升級版疫苗精準預防接種 - 生活 - 自由時報電子報
content: According to data from the Centers for Disease Control (CDC), the predominant serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae among Taiwan's population aged 65 and above have shifted significantly. Dr. Huang Jing-tai, a physician at Linkou Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, stated that the upcoming PCV20 vaccine will cover approximately 45% of serotypes, while the PCV21 vaccine will cover about 70%. The CDC's surveillance from 2021 to 2025 shows that the most common serotypes in older adults are 23A, 15A, 19A, 35B, and 3, with 23A, 15A, 35, 19A, and 23F being the primary causes of pneumonia-related deaths—where 23A and 15A are the most prevalent. Dr. Huang noted that PCV20 expands on PCV13 by adding seven serotypes, while PCV21 adds 17. The Taiwan Society of Infectious Diseases recommends adjusting adult pneumococcal vaccination strategies based on epidemiological trends and vaccine coverage. Dr. Zhang Feng-yi, president of the Taiwan Society of Infectious Diseases, emphasized that older adults with comorbidities such as diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, COPD, or chronic kidney disease face significantly higher risks of severe pneumonia, hospitalization, and death. He urged insurance providers in Taiwan to incentivize vaccination, noting that the U.S. Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) uses a risk-based approach, recommending vaccination for individuals with risk factors, with costs typically covered by insurance or out-of-pocket.

title: تطوير لقاح جديد ضد 21 سلالة من فيروس المكورات الرئوية - اليوم السابع
content: A new vaccine against 21 strains of pneumococcal disease is being developed in a joint international study. The study aims to provide greater protection for children against the common infection that causes pneumonia, otitis media, and meningitis. According to 'News medical life science', the study led by the Murdoch Children's Research Institute (MCRI) in Australia is evaluating a promising vaccine that protects against 21 strains of pneumococcal disease, compared to the current 13 strains included in the national immunization program. The Melbourne branch of the randomized controlled trial will test 50 families with healthy two-month-old children who have not received routine vaccinations. Participants will receive four doses of the vaccine at two months, four and a half months, and 12-15 months, in addition to all recommended childhood vaccinations in the national immunization plan (NIP). The study aims to enroll over 1600 children from Australia, the United States, Puerto Rico, Honduras, South Korea, and Thailand to ensure the vaccine's safety and ability to induce protective antibody responses in young children. Participants will be followed up for up to 19 months and will undergo three blood tests. Pneumococcal disease can cause severe illnesses and death in children under two years old. In 2024, 602 cases of invasive pneumococcal disease were reported in Victoria, including 373 cases among children aged 0-4 years. Dr. [no quote provided] said, 'This new vaccine has the potential to save more lives by protecting against 21 strains of pneumococcal disease.'

title: Vacina infantil contra pneumonia terá versão 'mais potente' no SUS a partir de 2026
content: Brazil’s National Immunization Program (PNI) announced that a new, more potent pneumococcal vaccine will be added to the SUS schedule in 2026. The current 10‑valent vaccine (Pncc10) protects against 10 serotypes and is given in three doses at 2, 4 and 12 months. Recent studies show that 264 invasive pneumococcal disease cases were reported in children ≤2 years in 2023‑24, and 92.3% of those cases in vaccinated children were caused by serotypes 19A and 3, indicating vaccine escape. PNI Director Éder Gatti said, 'Nos anos de 2023 e 2024, observamos 264 casos de doença pneumocócica invasiva em crianças de até 2 anos que tiveram oportunidade de se vacinar. Desse total, 92,3% dos casos em crianças vacinadas apenas com a Pncc10 foram provocados pelos sorotipos 19A e 3.' The new vaccine will cover these serotypes, and the government will adopt a flexible procurement strategy, allowing the PNI to switch between 13‑, 15‑, or 20‑valent formulations based on epidemiology. The new vaccine is expected to enter the national schedule in 2026, while families should continue the current schedule until then.

title: Pneumococcal Vaccine Market Opportunities and Strategies to 2034 - Pediatric Segment Holds the Major Opportunity in Market Expansion
content: The press release titled 'Pneumococcal Vaccine Market Opportunities and Strategies to 2034' reports that the global pneumococcal vaccine market was valued at $7.92 billion in 2024, growing at a CAGR of 4.17 % since 2019. Forecasts project the market to reach $10.04 billion by 2029 and $12.41 billion by 2034, with a CAGR of 4.33 % over 2024‑2034. North America dominated the 2024 market with 52.01 % ($4.12 billion); Asia‑Pacific and South America are expected to be the fastest‑growing regions, with CAGRs of 6.31 % and 5.71 % respectively. The market is highly concentrated, with Pfizer Inc. holding 82.01 % of the share, followed by Merck & Co., GlaxoSmithKline plc, and the Serum Institute of India Pvt. Ltd. Product segmentation shows that pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) accounted for 96.68 % ($7.66 billion) of the 2024 market and are projected to grow at a CAGR of 5.15 % through 2029. Intramuscular administration led the route segment with 99.17 % of the share in 2024 and is expected to maintain a 4.92 % CAGR to 2029. Public health agencies dominated distribution channels with 47.33 % of the share in 2024 and are projected to grow at a 6.68 % CAGR to 2029. End‑user analysis indicates pediatrics held 77.70 % of the market share in 2024, while the adult segment is projected to grow fastest at a CAGR of 6.74 %. The release highlights opportunities in the PCV and intramuscular segments, noting a projected $983.14 million increase in the U.S. market alone. Key trends include vaccine innovation, strategic collaborations, and broader serotype coverage, with companies encouraged to pursue region‑specific innovations, adult‑focused developments, and competitive pricing strategies.

title: Al via la Campagna vaccinale 2025-2026
content: The Apulia region launched the 2025-2026 influenza vaccination campaign on October 10, 2025, offering a combined vaccine that includes protection against influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcus, and herpes zoster (commonly known as 'Saint Anthony's fire'). The vaccine is available free of charge at general practitioners, pediatricians, ASL vaccination centers, and participating pharmacies. The region has acquired one million doses, already distributed to Prevention Departments, hospital directors, general practitioners, pediatricians, and local pharmacies to ensure broad and timely coverage. Priority is given to high-risk groups: individuals over 60, pregnant or postpartum women, children aged six months to six years, people with chronic conditions, residents of healthcare and social care facilities, family members of at-risk individuals, and professionals in healthcare, veterinary, essential services, and farming sectors. Medical professionals will also assess additional risk factors requiring protection. The campaign strongly recommends co-administering anti-COVID, anti-pneumococcal, and anti-herpes zoster vaccines. Additionally, Apulia continues its 2025-2026 program of administering monoclonal antibodies against Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), the leading cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants under one year. This initiative, successfully introduced last year, has already significantly reduced severe cases and hospitalizations among newborns. The campaign runs from October 10, 2025, to March 31, 2026, covering infants born between April 1, 2025, and March 31, 2026.

title: 21価肺炎球菌結合型ワクチンが承認、成人に特化した血清型を含有
content: Japan has approved a 21‑valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV21) that targets the serotypes most responsible for invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in adults. The vaccine contains 21 serotypes—3, 6A, 7F, 8, 9N, 10A, 11A, 12F, 15A, 15B‑o‑deacetylated, 16F, 17F, 19A, 20A, 22F, 23A, 23B, 24F, 31, 33F, and 35B—linked to the carrier protein CRM197. It adds eight serotypes (15A, 15B‑o‑deacetylated, 16F, 23A, 23B, 24F, 31, 35B) that are not covered by existing PCVs, thereby broadening protection. Clinical trials—including the domestic phase III 009 study, the overseas phase III 003 study, and the international phase III 008 study—confirmed the vaccine’s efficacy and safety. As of June 2025, the vaccine is approved in seven countries or regions (the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, Australia, the EU, the United Kingdom, and the UAE). Common adverse events reported are injection‑site pain (36.0 %), headache, and fatigue (each >10 %). Serious reactions such as shock or anaphylaxis are rare but possible. The vaccine is expected to provide wider protection against pneumococcal disease in adults compared with earlier PCVs. The article notes that "注射部位疼痛（36.0%）" and "頭痛、疲労（各10%以上）" are the main side‑effects, and that "ショック、アナフィラキシーの可能性がある" should be taken into account.

title: لقاح جديد مضاد للبكتيريا الرئوية
content: A clinical study by 'Merck' showed that the new pneumococcal vaccine Capvaxive elicits strong and effective immune responses in children and adolescents aged 2‑18 with chronic illnesses or immunodeficiency, outperforming the older PPSV23 vaccine. The study, which included participants up to 18 years old, demonstrated that Capvaxive covers a wide range of pneumococcal serotypes responsible for pneumonia, meningitis, and sepsis—diseases that pose a serious threat to vulnerable populations. Safety data indicated no serious adverse events during the trial, supporting the likelihood of future regulatory approval. Researchers suggest that incorporating Capvaxive into national immunization programs could markedly reduce respiratory disease burden, lower mortality, and decrease hospital admissions, especially in communities lacking robust health systems or facing high rates of antibiotic‑resistant bacterial infections.
